citations.authors: C. N. Yang and R. L. Mills
citations.limitation: It is a classical field-theoretic origin paper, not a constructive quantum existence or mass-gap proof.
citations.supports: Introduces non-abelian gauge fields and the classical Yang-Mills object that later becomes the quantum target.
citations.title: Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance

literature_stages.core_shift: Yang and Mills replace an abelian electromagnetic-style gauge field with a nonlinear non-abelian gauge field.
literature_stages.title: The non-abelian gauge object is born
literature_stages.what_became_possible: The target object becomes a rich classical field theory with compact gauge-group structure.
literature_stages.what_remained_open: There is still no rigorous quantum field theory, no Hilbert space, and no mass-gap statement.

citations.authors: R. F. Streater and A. S. Wightman
citations.limitation: It supplies the standard to satisfy; it does not construct four-dimensional Yang-Mills.
citations.supports: Provides the Wightman-style axiomatic target standard for relativistic quantum field theory.
citations.title: PCT, Spin and Statistics, and All That
citations.venue: W. A. Benjamin; later Princeton University Press

citations.limitation: The theorem gives a reconstruction criterion; Yang-Mills still needs Schwinger functions satisfying the hypotheses in the continuum limit.
citations.supports: Turns Euclidean Schwinger-function control, especially reflection positivity, into a route toward Wightman reconstruction.
citations.title: Axioms for Euclidean Green's Functions I-II

literature_stages.core_shift: Wightman axioms set a Lorentzian QFT standard; Osterwalder-Schrader theory makes Euclidean Schwinger functions a possible reconstruction route.
literature_stages.title: The rigor standard becomes axiomatic and Euclidean
literature_stages.what_became_possible: A proof can aim at Euclidean objects, but only if reflection positivity, covariance, regularity, clustering, and reconstruction hypotheses are preserved.
literature_stages.what_remained_open: The Yang-Mills Schwinger functions still have to be constructed nonperturbatively in four dimensions.

citations.authors: D. J. Gross and F. Wilczek
citations.limitation: Perturbative ultraviolet control does not by itself construct the full theory or prove a positive mass gap.
citations.supports: Asymptotic freedom explains why non-abelian gauge theory can be weakly coupled at short distance while remaining nonperturbative in the infrared.
citations.title: Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories

citations.limitation: It motivates the short-distance regime; it does not solve infrared confinement or the constructive problem.
citations.supports: Independent asymptotic-freedom result reinforcing the ultraviolet side of the Yang-Mills/QCD picture.
citations.title: Reliable Perturbative Results for Strong Interactions?

citations.limitation: Strong-coupling lattice confinement is not the same as a continuum four-dimensional Clay-problem proof.
citations.supports: Introduces lattice gauge theory and strong-coupling confinement mechanisms that make a mass gap physically plausible.
citations.title: Confinement of Quarks

literature_stages.core_shift: The literature clarifies the ultraviolet/infrared split: perturbation theory can work at short distances, while lattice strong coupling suggests confinement and massive glueball-like excitations.
literature_stages.title: Asymptotic freedom and lattice confinement reshape expectations
literature_stages.what_became_possible: The problem stops looking physically arbitrary: a gap is expected, and lattice regularization gives concrete finite systems to analyze.
literature_stages.what_remained_open: Short-distance perturbation and strong-coupling lattice arguments do not bridge to the continuum Clay target by themselves.

citations.limitation: The classic constructive successes do not include a full four-dimensional Yang-Mills solution.
citations.supports: Shows what rigorous constructive quantum field theory can look like and why existence is a mathematical construction problem, not only a physics argument.
citations.title: Quantum Physics: A Functional Integral Point of View

citations.limitation: It clarifies the program and obstacles rather than closing the four-dimensional continuum mass-gap problem.
citations.supports: Frames gauge theories as constructive field-theory and statistical-mechanics problems with lattice-to-continuum pressure.
citations.title: Gauge Theories as a Problem of Constructive Quantum Field Theory and Statistical Mechanics

citations.limitation: Ultraviolet stability and related RG control still need same-theory continuum construction, nontriviality, and spectral-gap witnesses.
citations.supports: Represents a rigorous renormalization-group route toward ultraviolet stability for lattice gauge theories.
citations.title: Ultraviolet Stability of Three-Dimensional Lattice Pure Gauge Field Theories

literature_stages.core_shift: The literature shows that existence means constructing measures, Schwinger functions, limits, and reconstruction data with uniform control, not merely writing a path integral.
literature_stages.title: Constructive QFT and RG expose the real mathematical bottleneck
literature_stages.what_became_possible: Balaban-style RG and constructive-field methods give a disciplined route language: cutoffs, ultraviolet stability, lattice-to-continuum control, and limiting objects.
literature_stages.what_remained_open: The full four-dimensional continuum Yang-Mills object, nontriviality, OS/Wightman adequacy, and positive spectral gap remain coupled obligations.

citations.limitation: It defines the target and admissible rigor standard; it is not a solution.
citations.supports: Gives the Clay target: construct nontrivial quantum Yang-Mills on four-dimensional space and prove a positive mass gap for compact simple gauge group.
citations.title: Quantum Yang-Mills Theory
citations.venue: Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Problem statement

citations.limitation: It is a status report, not a proof or definitive taxonomy of all later approaches.
citations.supports: Explains the status and difficulty of turning physical Yang-Mills understanding into a rigorous Millennium-problem solution.
citations.title: Report on the Status of the Yang-Mills Millennium Prize Problem

literature_stages.core_shift: The problem becomes a same-theory requirement: construct the nontrivial theory and prove the positive gap for that reconstructed theory.
literature_stages.title: The Clay formulation fuses construction and mass gap into one target
literature_stages.what_became_possible: Discovery work can be audited against explicit commitments: existence, nontriviality, OS/Wightman adequacy, continuum limit, and positive mass gap.
literature_stages.what_remained_open: Most proposed routes risk solving a regulated, perturbative, lower-dimensional, numerical, or proxy problem unless same-theory transfer is certified.

open_obligations: Construct continuum Schwinger functions or equivalent fields for the same Yang-Mills object.
Preserve reflection positivity and reconstruction hypotheses in the limit.
Show nontriviality rather than collapse to a free, Gaussian, empty, or proxy theory.
Turn Euclidean decay or Hamiltonian estimates into a positive spectral gap for the reconstructed physical Hilbert space.
Certify that all steps refer to the same compact-simple-gauge Yang-Mills theory on four-dimensional space.

problem_statement.accessible: Construct a nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills theory for every compact simple gauge group and prove a strictly positive mass gap.

solution_criteria: The quantum Yang-Mills theory must be constructed, not postulated.
The theory must be nontrivial and satisfy axioms at least as strong as the Wightman/OS standard required by the Clay formulation.
The continuum limit must preserve the same gauge theory and observable algebra.
The Hamiltonian or equivalent reconstructed spectral object must have no non-vacuum spectrum arbitrarily close to zero.
why_it_matters: It asks for the first complete nonperturbative construction of a physically central four-dimensional interacting quantum gauge theory.
It would turn the physicists' confinement and glueball mass-gap picture into a theorem in a reconstructed quantum field theory.
It is a stress test for whether constructive QFT, Euclidean reconstruction, lattice gauge theory, and renormalization can meet in one same-theory proof.

workflow_implications.active_workflow_effect: Branch ranking should reward calculations that state source object, target object, cutoff regime, and continuum handoff.
workflow_implications.lesson: Every promising finite or lattice calculation must carry a same-theory transfer certificate.

workflow_implications.active_workflow_effect: OS/reflection-positivity branches should remain central, but only when they keep reconstruction assumptions explicit.
workflow_implications.lesson: Euclidean positivity is not a cosmetic condition; it is the bridge from Schwinger data to Hilbert-space spectral claims.

workflow_implications.active_workflow_effect: The loop should avoid mistaking perturbative UV success for nonperturbative continuum construction.
workflow_implications.lesson: Asymptotic freedom controls the ultraviolet story but leaves the infrared gap and construction problem alive.

workflow_implications.active_workflow_effect: Next analyses should prefer bounded estimates, falsifiers, and bridge lemmas over broad route enthusiasm.
workflow_implications.lesson: Constructive/RG work teaches that uniform estimates and limiting objects are the proof currency.
